utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I see you without support.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. We seem to be a football team down a couple of our players, a substantial number, as a matter of fact. I received a telephone call this late morning from the Detention Unit indicating that my client was being taken to the hospital. Apparently something is amiss; as I think the Trial Chamber is aware, he does have pre-existing medical conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no specific information at all with regard to what the problem is; however I believe it is a continuation of the pre-existing cardiac difficulties. That's what I have been led to believe. I was told that there have been incidents. However the people in the Detention Unit felt that the severity of this incident was such that it was prudent and appropriate to take him to the hospital. That is the beginning and the end of the information that I have at this time with regard to his present physical condition. I am not in a position, obviously, in his absence to do much with regard to working in this particular field. In other fields I can outside of court, but whilst he is absent, at least for the moment, I am not able to proceed. And I apologise to the Court. However I think of all the days that such a thing could occur perhaps this is not a bad day since we're already short in other respects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the actual standard of things may be lifting. It seems quite obvious, given the circumstances, that it would be inappropriate to continue the hearing today. And clearly, it will be necessary if there is to be any continuation of your client's ill health to get some information as to the prognosis so that we can make an assessment from the point of view of the trial's continuance. I think, Mr. Whiting, the inevitable is that we must adjourn today. I know this would inconvenience you and your witness, but it seems in the circumstances unavoidable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, I certainly concur with that, and as Mr. Guy-Smith said, it was a short day anyhow so it falls well -- of course as the Court indicated, if it continues we'll have to take up the matter. I don't know if the Court wishes to bring the witness in to advise the witness about what's happened or have the witness unit do that. It's the Court's preference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Whiting. There was the matter of legal submissions, but it would seem that that probably ought to be left as well, Mr. Guy-Smith, for the same reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would think so, Your Honour. At this point I'll hold off until the next time that we're all together, if that's amenable to the Trial Chamber. There is one other matter which is: I don't know whether or not there's going to be any contact between the Detention Unit and the Trial Chamber with regard to Mr. Bala's condition. I will endeavour to get information and any information I get I will forward to all parties immediately. But I also would hope that perhaps the Detention Unit, because sometimes the lines of communication are perhaps a bit more direct, might be able to inform the Trial Chamber with regard to my client's status just so we have a second way of checking that. Part of my concern is as follows. I don't know whether or not he's in such a condition that we're going to have to be in his absence again tomorrow. And if that does occur, I don't know what the Chamber's thinking is, whether the Chamber wishes to wait until we reached that issue or not because I may need to take some instruction from him if I can find out where he is in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The first step would be whether -- if there is to be any prolonged break in his ability to be present, whether the trial might continue with his agreement on the basis that you'll be here representing his interest. And that's a matter about which you would obviously need to seek instructions. If he does not consent to the trial continuing, the Chamber will have to look into the question of whether regardless of that there should be some continuation of the proceedings and that would involve some reliable information as to the medical condition and the likely length of time of absence and the like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that's all contingent at the moment. We will hope for every reason that your client recovers quickly and can attend again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I leave it with you to pursue seeking that information and, if necessary, instructions. The Chamber will routinely receive some information, but I think you would get more detailed instruction through your client than the Chamber would. We will see. Mr. Topolski, are you wishing to say something? I just saw you looking as though you might have a contribution to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon. That's all I can usefully add to the proceedings. Your Honours know I perhaps ought to simply add this for the record: that Mr. Limaj is without both Mr. Mansfield and Mr. Khan today. With your leave, I regard myself as protecting his interests at Mr. Mansfield's request and at his confirmation that I may do that. And he has nothing to add to the discussions that Your Honours had with Mr. Guy-Smith, nor for that matter does Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the first instance we must adjourn with a view to hoping that the accused is in a position to be back in court, and if not, for instructions from him to be obtained by his counsel, which means at the earliest we will continue tomorrow. That would be at 2.15. That will be our adjournment, but if information is received that makes it clear that we cannot continue tomorrow, there will have to be a telephone communication to let you know of that if that's convenient. If the witness could be brought in. I think as a matter of courtesy we should explain the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Qeriqi, unfortunately one of the three accused men has developed some medical condition and has had to be taken to hospital; because of that, we will not be able to continue the hearing today. We hope that he will be in a position to return to the court tomorrow. For that reason, unfortunately, we must advise you that we will not be hearing any more of your evidence today but we'll hope to be able to continue with your evidence tomorrow at 2.15. I am sorry for that inconvenience, but as you can understand if an accused man is ill, well then he needs to receive his medical treatment and we must wait while that is done. So with that apology, we will now adjourn for the day to resume hopefully tomorrow at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: [The accused Limaj and Musliu entered court]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.30 p.m.,
